sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page deng1250 (Dengese) and search pages for 'Ohendo' and 'Indanga'
sources.note: Classification only; confirms Ohendo is a separate language (song1305) and that no languoid named Indanga exists (Motingea 1992 Indanga is filed under deng1250).

sources.citation: Annales Aequatoria 24 (2003) [whole volume; Nollet, Conflict and subversion in the Central Congo 1920-1940, pp. 77-96 mentions the Dengese territory]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: downloaded while locating the Indanga article (it is in vol. 23); only historical mentions of the Dengese; no linguistic content.

sources.citation: Jacobs, John & Barthélemy Omeonga. 2002. Texte et lexique indanga (Kɔlɔmɔnyi, Kɔlɛ, Kasaï Oriental). Annales Aequatoria 23: 537-552.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. The only prosodic remark (p. 538) is one sentence on 'accent musical' (tone): the tone melody of some words changes after a preceding final high tone (nkɔi > nkɔ́i 'léopard' in mǎ nkɔ́i). Lexicon (pp. 548-552) sorts verb radicals by tone (ton bas / ton haut). Data from 1954 fieldwork at Kolomonyi (Kole); Indanga is assigned to deng1250 by Glottolog via Motingea 1992.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Esquisse du parler des Ohendo. Annales Aequatoria 11: 115-152.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: NOT deng1250: Ohendo = Songomeno (song1305, ISO soe), the Ndengese's neighbour (Guthrie grouped it with Kuba; Motingea places it with Nkundo-Mongo). §'Tonologie et syllabation' p. 122: tones and syllable types 'respectent l'allure générale des parlers môngo'; elided-syllable tone projects onto the next syllable. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hulstaert, Gustave. 1985. Les langues kuba et mongo. Annales Aequatoria 6: 87-106.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative Kuba/Mongo wordlists with Ndengese forms; tone is mentioned only comparatively (p. 105: Kuba tonality 'apparait semblable au système môngo'); nothing on stress or accent for Ndengese. Bibliography p. 104 lists Goemaere 1942 Woordenlijst londengɛsɛ (Dumba) and Goemaere 1984.

sources.citation: [Recensions notice] Hulstaert, G. & A. Goemaere (†). 1984. Grammaire du londengese (Publications CEEBA III/11). Notice in Annales Aequatoria 6 (1985): 246-247.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic notice only: the 1984 grammar is Hulstaert's French translation of Goemaere's 1940 Dutch manuscript 'Spraakleer van het Londengese', modelled on Hulstaert's Praktische Grammatika van het Lonkundo (1938); base dialect that of the Ngɛl'e Njale and Weko in the Lokenye basin. No content on stress given.

sources.citation: Hulstaert, Gustave. 1951. [Classification of Mongo dialects, entry 'Groupe 80. 81. Ndengese.'] Aequatoria 14: 24.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Five-line classificatory note only (Ndengese is a Mongo dialect, close to Loyajima, Lombole and Lonkutu; sub-dialects by sub-tribe); nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1992. Le parler des Indanga: un des dialectes móngo les plus méridionaux. In E. W. Müller & A.-M. sources.note: Motingea's sketches (cf. his 1990 Ohendo sketch) have a phonetics/tonology section; this is the Glottolog-listed sketch of the Indanga variety filed under deng1250 and would supersede the Jacobs & Omeonga tone note.
